title: The BMC cannot be reached over IPMI
status: unreviewed: first estimates by Claude on 2026-11-08, not yet reviewed by the author

causes.title: ipmi_devintf is not loaded, so /dev/ipmi0 is never created
causes.why: the device node comes from ipmi_devintf; distros do not always load it automatically.

causes.title: ipmi_si found no BMC interface (or none registered)
causes.why: if the system interface does not probe (BIOS/ACPI tables, KCS address), there is nothing to talk to.

causes.title: /dev/ipmi0 exists but only root can open it
causes.why: the device is root-only by default; the probe runs unprivileged.

causes.title: Both modules are loaded but the device node was not created
causes.why: the interface registered after ipmi_devintf, or udev/devtmpfs did not create the node.

causes.title: The BMC (IMM) itself is hung
causes.why: an IMM that stops answering makes every IPMI call fail; rare, fixed by an IMM reset.

evidence.title: No IPMI device node exists
evidence.why: a missing node rules out a permission problem and points at the driver chain.

evidence.title: Opening the IPMI device was denied
evidence.why: the node exists; only access is the issue.

evidence.title: ipmi_devintf is loaded
evidence.why: with the module present, a missing node needs another explanation.

evidence.title: ipmi_si is loaded
evidence.why: the driver loaded, though it may still have found no interface.
